claim_boundary: C017 removes two invalid shortcuts and adds four narrower descendants. None resolves P versus NP or is promoted to PROVED.

hypotheses.title: Contextual Circuit-Frege Upper-Bound Lemma Candidate
hypotheses.statement: Let a fixed finite library contain equivalent constant-size circuit pairs (A_j,B_j), each with a constant-size Circuit-Frege proof of equivalence. For every polynomial-size acyclic circuit context Comp_n using these pairs at designated ports, the circuits C_n=Comp_n(A_j) and D_n=Comp_n(B_j) have polynomial-size Circuit-Frege proofs of equivalence obtained bottom-up with one constant-cost congruence derivation per DAG gate. Consequently Krajicek's exact local rewrite relation admits a polynomial-length chain from C_n to D_n.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: H111 is impossible, and any H110 endpoint family must have globally proof-hard equivalence rather than arise from transparent amplification of a fixed EF-easy gadget library.
hypotheses.proof_role: DIRECT_BRIDGE: turn the Circuit-Frege closure of polynomial DAG contexts into an explicit upper bound on the rewrite distance targeted by H111.
hypotheses.next_gate: Obtain independent proof review and state the exact polynomial bound under one fixed Circuit-Frege encoding and the R038 simulation exponent.
hypotheses.delta_from_parents: H117 reverses H111's proposed amplification: polynomial-size contextual composition of fixed locally equivalent gadgets yields a polynomial proof and therefore a polynomial rewrite chain.
falsification_conditions: A polynomial-size acyclic context for which bottom-up congruence requires superpolynomial Circuit-Frege size.
A failure of the exact R038 theorem to translate the resulting polynomial proof into a polynomial rewrite chain.
A hidden nonlocal port operation outside ordinary circuit composition.
hypotheses.claim_boundary: The lemma does not upper-bound rewrite distance for endpoint equivalences lacking polynomial-size compositional proofs.

hypotheses.title: Exact XOR-Cycle Local SAT-UNSAT Twin Lemma Candidate
hypotheses.statement: For every fixed radius R there are explicit polynomial-time constructible 2-CNF formulas S_R and U_R on two equal variable cycles such that S_R is satisfiable, U_R is unsatisfiable, their complete multisets of rooted signed incidence neighborhoods through radius R are exactly equal, and both primal graphs have treewidth at most two. S_R places two inequality edges in one cycle and none in the other; U_R places one inequality edge in each cycle, with cycle length 8R+12.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: The local-twin construction component sought by H114 exists even in 2-CNF, but it cannot by itself obstruct low-treewidth global algorithms because component parity remains visible in the global assembly.
hypotheses.proof_role: ADVERSARIAL_TARGET: separate exact local indistinguishability from the missing global-assembly theorem by an explicit parity-cycle family.
hypotheses.next_gate: Obtain independent verification of the universal neighborhood-count argument and use the family as a regression test for every proposed locality-to-global transfer.
hypotheses.delta_from_parents: H118 supplies exact opposite-label local twins but deliberately keeps treewidth two, exposing the precise global-assembly information omitted by H115.
falsification_conditions: A radius R for which the rooted signed-neighborhood multisets differ.
A satisfying assignment for U_R or failure of the explicit assignment for S_R.
A primal edge outside the two cycles or treewidth greater than two.
hypotheses.claim_boundary: The family is not a lower bound against H106; the identity compiler already produces treewidth-two outputs and a global DP distinguishes the pair.

hypotheses.title: High-Treewidth Lift Factorization Obstruction Conjecture
hypotheses.statement: For every fixed pass bound q and radius r, there are explicit high-treewidth signed CNF lift pairs with opposite satisfiability and a common radius-qr covering structure such that every isomorphism-invariant H106 transduction whose output has polynomial size and O(log n) treewidth must factor through a common bounded quotient on both lifts. The quotient factorization erases the global parity distinguishing the pair, so no such transduction can be equisatisfiable with local witness recovery.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: H106 is refuted for a reason that survives the H118 counterexample: the input is too high-treewidth for identity, and every allowed low-treewidth output is forced to forget the decisive lift parity.
hypotheses.proof_role: ADVERSARIAL_BRIDGE: replace H115's false local-type inventory transfer by a covering-preserving global factorization theorem that explicitly controls output assembly.
hypotheses.next_gate: Construct one explicit high-treewidth XOR or Tseitin lift pair and prove a low-treewidth factorization theorem for the exact constant-pass transduction syntax of H106.
hypotheses.delta_from_parents: H119 adds the two missing resources exposed by H118: high input treewidth to exclude identity and a common-quotient theorem controlling the entire output graph rather than only local type counts.
falsification_conditions: An H106-legal low-treewidth transduction preserving the global lift parity without violating radius-qr ancestry.
Failure of the proposed pair to have opposite satisfiability or common local covering structure.
A low-treewidth output that does not factor through the claimed quotient.
hypotheses.claim_boundary: No factorization theorem or explicit high-treewidth pair satisfying all clauses is currently known.

hypotheses.title: SAT-Sound Witness-Cover Upper-Bound Lemma Candidate
hypotheses.statement: For any padded positive SAT list T={(F_i,a_i)} on a fixed canonical CNF input shape, let A_T be the set of distinct listed assignments. The circuit C_T(F)=OR_{a in A_T}[a satisfies F] is globally SAT-sound, accepts every formula in T, and has size O(|A_T| times e(L,v)), where e(L,v) is the polynomial size of a fixed-assignment evaluator for encoding length L and v variables. Hence an H116 list hitting every sound circuit of size n^k must satisfy |A_T|e(L,v)>n^k up to fixed encoding constants.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: H116 cannot succeed through repeated formulas or a small common witness set; its constructor must create target-scale witness diversity and still defeat every semantic compression beyond the explicit witness cover.
hypotheses.proof_role: DIRECT_BRIDGE: make the universal hardcoded-witness attack on positive SAT lists exact and charge it against the H116 circuit budget.
hypotheses.next_gate: Fix one canonical variable-length encoding, prove the evaluator gate bound, and search for a list whose positive region is incompressible by sound circuits beyond witness-union coverage.
hypotheses.delta_from_parents: H120 converts C016's informal hardcoded-list warning into a globally SAT-sound circuit construction parameterized by distinct witness assignments and an explicit size upper bound.
falsification_conditions: A listed formula not accepted by the union of its listed witness evaluators.
A formula accepted by the cover circuit despite being unsatisfiable.
A fixed-shape CNF evaluation model requiring superpolynomial circuit size.
hypotheses.claim_boundary: The lemma gives a necessary condition only and does not construct H116 anti-checkers or prove a circuit lower bound.
